Tom (Customer): Hey — our rerank responses suddenly show values like -23.4, -0.5, -5.1 for the same batch of candidates. We expected 0..1 probabilities. Using model: rwd/rerank-base-001 via v1/rerank. Sample response snippet: {
  "candidates": [{"text": "Billing", "score": -23.4}, {"text": "Pricing", "score": -0.5}, {"text": "Support", "score": -5.1} ]
}
Can you confirm what these scores represent and whether they should be normalized? Also noticed a token usage spike on billing for these calls.

Aisha (CS): Hi Tom — thanks for the report. Can you paste the exact request (headers + body) you used and the SDK version? Any query params or options (e.g., normalize flag) are helpful. :mag:

Tom (Customer): Repro below (redacted token):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"query":"How do I update billing?","candidates":["Billing terms","Pricing","Support"],"options":{"normalize_scores":false}}'
```
We call this via our SDK 0.9.0 and explicitly set options.normalize_scores=false because we thought the SDK normalized by default historically.

Tom (Customer): Full response truncated: {
  "candidates": [
    {"text": "Billing terms", "score": -23.4},
    {"text": "Pricing", "score": -0.5},
    {"text": "Support", "score": -5.1}
  ]
}

Sam (ML Eng): Hey — heads-up: rerank returns model-specific score semantics. For many models the raw output is a logit-like score (not probabilities) so negative/large-magnitude values are expected. If you want probabilities between 0..1 you should either:
- set options.normalize_scores=true (server-side normalization), OR
- apply softmax client-side to the returned scores.

Quick softmax example on your three logits: [-23.4, -0.5, -5.1] -> subtract max (-0.5) => [-22.9, 0, -4.6]. exp -> [~1.1e-10, 1, ~0.01005]. Sum ~ 1.01005. Probabilities ~= [~1e-10, 0.990, 0.00995]. So the middle candidate dominates once normalized.

Sam (ML Eng): Note: historically some older rerank variants returned normalized scores by default; we recently changed defaults for consistency with other endpoints which led to raw logit outputs unless normalize_scores is true. That explains the surprise.

Aisha (CS): Sorry about the churn — that change should have been in the changelog. We can do two things immediately:
1) For your org we can flip a per-customer flag so responses are normalized server-side for your production run (temporary).
2) Long term we'll add a clearer parameter (score_output: "prob" | "logit") and update SDKs.

Dev Support Bot: Created ticket CS-7893 for Tom (Customer) and linked INF-1421 (feature request).

Tom (Customer): Would appreciate a server-side normalization toggle for now — we can't ship a quick client fix to all downstream services today. Also please confirm whether billing tokens are counted differently for normalized vs raw outputs (we saw a spike).

Sam (ML Eng): We'll normalize server-side for your org as a stop-gap. Billing note: normalization is a cheap post-processing step; it should not materially change token counts. The token spike may be unrelated — we'll audit request logs for content length and retry storms.

Sam (ML Eng): I've filed INF-1421 to add explicit score_output param and SDKs update. I'll also open a small PR to restore old behavior behind a compatibility flag in the SDK.

Aisha (CS): Action plan:
- Sam: enable per-org normalization toggle (one-off) and verify with 2 example batches from Tom.
- Support: audit billing anomalies for thread CS-7893.
- Product/Docs: add a short note about rerank score semantics and the normalize_scores flag.

Tom (Customer): Thanks — attaching two sample batches in the ticket now. Appreciate the quick help. :pray:

Aisha (CS): Closing the immediate loop here — we'll update CS-7893 with timeline. If you need an explicit SLA on score semantics for Dedicated/Private deployments we can scope that in the feature ticket.
